target_customer: Data center builders and operators, and electrical and electronics manufacturers needing skilled manual work
problem: Skilled physical work such as wiring, kitting, inspection and commissioning in data centers and factories is variable and dexterous, so traditional automation struggles and labor is short.
business_model: Robot deployment with integration into customer workflows, pricing not public
product_category: General purpose robots, robot foundation models

founders.name: Feifei Duan
founders.background_notes: YC page: trained large transformer models at Waymo and deployed robots into food factories at Chef Robotics.

founders.name: David Fang
founders.background_notes: YC page: research scientist at Dyna Robotics, ML for autonomous driving at Cruise.

founders.name: Kai Ru
founders.background_notes: YC page: planning tech lead at Cruise, then multimodal foundation models at Rivian.

competitors.name: Watney Robotics
competitors.funding_then: $80M Series A per a Dealroom news note, date not confirmed

technical_complexity.rationale: General purpose manipulation with foundation models across variable wiring and assembly tasks is research grade, and the team had only a few members at launch.

defensibility.rationale: Real world and simulation training data could compound, but no deployments or data advantage is documented and well funded rivals target the same sites.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Several funded companies already pursue data center robots. No Shepherd specific response is public.

market_need_then: AI data center construction is expanding fast in 2026 and press describes robots entering construction and maintenance, with labor bottlenecks cited by operators.

identity.visual_style: Minimal landing page with only a title and tagline

brand_strength.rationale: Brand is brand new, with only a one line site and one launch article found.

outcome_analysis: Shepherd joined YC in Fall 2026 and launched in October 2026 without disclosing deployment counts, customer names or production performance. It has no exit or failure. Its founders come from Waymo, Cruise and robotics startups, which fits the task, but it enters data center robotics where Watney and others were already funded, so traction after demo day is the open question.
notes: Funding unverified: Dealroom shows a $125k seed, but the same figure appears on another YC company's Dealroom page so it may be a template value, and no investors are named. No round recorded. Education was not listed on any source opened. Competitor dates are approximate to 2026.
